messages:
maria_sec: FYI detection: sudden sustained traffic spike hitting api.prod.redwood.ai frontends (IPv6-heavy). Observed mix of UDP/QUIC probes + HTTP/2 flood, total ~120-140k rps, health checks and client timeouts rising. Marking as incident and escalating to SRE + NetOps.
ash_sre: On it. Can you paste the flow aggregates/ASNs? need to know if it's one cloud provider or many.
maria_sec: Aggregates show top source ASN: 64512, but ~70% from ephemeral IPv6 prefixes across multiple ASNs. Pattern: large number of short-lived connections with small payloads.
kevin_netops: Sounds like a volumetric IPv6 UDP/QUIC amplification + stream opens. I'll validate with our edge telemetry. Suggest immediate edge rate-limits + WAF geo/ASN blocking where safe.
devon_prod: Impact: elevated 5xx rates on generation endpoints (~10% failure), latency up ~2.3x for p95. A few customer support tickets coming in.
jin_support: I already messaged top 5 paying customers that might be affected. Will provide updates after we confirm mitigations.
ash_sre: Plan: 1) apply per-route emergency rate limit at edge for /v1/generate 2) push WAF rule to block malformed HTTP/2 frames + QUIC probes 3) enable additional request tagging and pcap sampling for forensic capture. Need Sec approval for any RBAC emergency change?
maria_sec: Emergency RBAC: I authorized temporary role elevation for ash_sre and kevin_netops for 30m to apply edge rules. All changes will be logged. Audit logging already on for the control plane.
kevin_netops: Applying temporary rate-limit now: `edgectl rate-limit set --route /v1/generate --limit 500rps --scope per-ip --duration 600s`
deploy-bot: edge-proxy-1 rate-limit updated by kevin_netops at 2023-12-05T15:12:08Z. Rule id: rl-9f3a.
ash_sre: Also pushed WAF snippet to staging then prod. Rule (pseudocode):
```
if request.protocol == "http2" and request.flags == "malformed" then block
if connection.protocol == "quic" and request.size < 64 and req.rate > 200 then challenge
```
Pushed to prod ruleset rs-edge-uptime-2023-7.
deploy-bot: WAF rule rs-edge-uptime-2023-7 deployed to all edge clusters at 2023-12-05T15:14:01Z.
ash_sre: Traffic dropped from 130k rps to ~3k rps after rate-limit + WAF. 5xxs falling, p95 latency returning toward baseline.
devon_prod: Thanks — starting customer update draft. Keep me posted if we need to escalate to status.redwood.ai notice.
maria_sec: Forensics: please capture pcap samples and augment logs with `x-edge-src-ip6` header for later correlation. Save any changed rules and note audit IDs (rl-9f3a, rs-edge-uptime-2023-7).
kevin_netops: Captures started. Also triaging whether a BGP blackhole is warranted for ASN 64512 ranges — leaning toward selective blackhole for most abusive prefixes.
sam_roster: I've opened an incident ticket in PagerDuty (INC-20231205-121) and assigned post-incident owner to ash_sre. Scheduling 1h postmortem tomorrow.
jin_support: Sent targeted updates to affected customers with mitigation ETA. No billing credits recommended at this stage, will re-evaluate if there are persistent outages.
maria_sec: Post-incident actions (high level): 1) Add default IPv6-rate-limit baseline on edge to reduce blast radius 2) Expand WAF rules for malformed http2/quic probes 3) Update RBAC emergency playbook to document temporary elevation steps and audit checks 4) Add automated detector for connection-churn-from-new-prefixes.
nash_sre: Agreed. I'll open PRs for the playbook updates and the edge default config.
kevin_netops: Also: evaluate KMS access patterns for edge certificates — ensure no key material event coincided. No indication yet but will confirm.
maria_sec: Closing active mitigation — traffic stable and under thresholds. Incident moving to post-incident state. Please attach any logs, pcap, and rule diffs to the incident ticket.
deploy-bot: Incident INC-20231205-121 status changed to "mitigated" by ash_sre at 2023-12-05T15:28:30Z.
ash_sre: Quick note: RBAC elevation duration logged. We revoked temporary roles at 15:30 UTC. Audit entries: audit-9876543.
maria_sec: Thanks team. We'll run the postmortem and include remediation timelines.
devon_prod: Drafting customer-facing postmortem now; will coordinate language with security.
jin_support: Triage done on tickets — closing duplicates, keeping a watchlist for reopen if customers report further issues.
sam_roster: PM to schedule tabletop and action owner sync for the follow-ups.
maria_sec: End of thread.
